runbooks.diagnosis: OpenCloud 6.0.0 had a startup data race with default GOMAXPROCS on multi-core hosts; the fix in this stack is GOMAXPROCS=1 for the startup phase. If the env var was dropped in an image bump, the race returns.
remediation: Verify GOMAXPROCS=1 is set in the opencloud service environment
Check the oc_notifications/oc_* SMTP env names have the OC_ prefix where required
Restart opencloud after the env fix

runbooks.diagnosis: The S3/Garage backend env (endpoint, bucket, credentials) is misconfigured. In this stack opencloud may use the built-in ocis (local FS) backend instead — a mixed config (some services on S3, some local) surfaces as missing files after a restart.
remediation: Confirm which storage backend the current config selects (OC_* storage env)
If S3: verify bucket exists and credentials work from inside the container
Do NOT switch backends on a populated instance without a migration

runbooks.diagnosis: OpenCloud's OIDC issuer URL must be the externally reachable IdM URL, not the internal service name — token validation happens against the issuer metadata.
remediation: Set the OIDC issuer to the public IdM URL
Ensure opencloud can reach that URL from inside the compose network (hairpin NAT or split DNS)

runbooks.diagnosis: The nix-built opencloud image symlinks /etc/passwd and /etc/group into /nix/store; docker >= 29 exec walks them with openat2 RESOLVE_BENEATH and rejects the symlinks — every docker exec and in-container healthcheck fails (rc=126) while the app itself serves fine.
remediation: Use the execfix image build (opencloud/execfix/): COPY real passwd/group files into /etc/ from a plain FROM base — no RUN step, since RUN itself needs exec
Rebuild opensme-opencloud:9.1.0-nix-execfix and redeploy
Or set the opencloud healthcheck to none and rely on external monitoring (edge static IP)

runbooks.diagnosis: OpenCloud 8.x aligned the proxy/auth-basic/graph/idm bind passwords implicitly; 9.x generates per-service values when left unset — so the bind is rejected and every basic-auth login 401s. Stack-side automated binders (e.g. umfragen-bot) did not survive the 8→9 idm migration.
remediation: Pin all binders explicitly (OC_ADMIN_PASSWORD and the idm/proxy/auth-basic bind envs) in the opencloud service environment
Recreate the affected bot account via the Graph API (stack-specific)
Verify a basic-auth login returns 200, not 401

runbooks.diagnosis: A fresh demo boot can crash two ways: (1) storage-users (ocis driver) uses metadata prefix user.ocis. while storage-system defaults to user.oc. → 'metadata prefix is already set' panic; (2) the notifications service fatally validates an empty NOTIFICATIONS_SMTP_SENDER at startup (the live stack sets it via .env, the demo profile doesn't).
remediation: Set OC_METADATA_PREFIX: user.ocis. for the demo/fresh profile
Provide NOTIFICATIONS_SMTP_SENDER (+ HOST/PORT/AUTHENTICATION/TLS_INSECURE) defaults for fresh boots
Recreate the service for fresh (non-persisted config volume) boots after the env fix

runbooks.diagnosis: The demo profile pinned OC_URL to http://... while the edge serves :443 — the ocis proxy answers / with 404 because the configured proxy URL scheme doesn't match the request. The OIDC issuer must stay https (OpenCloud refuses plain-http issuers).
remediation: Set OC_URL: https://${OPENCLOUD_DOMAIN} when the edge terminates :443
Keep OC_OIDC_ISSUER on https
Recreate opencloud after the env change

symptoms: no configured subnet contains ip address
runbooks.diagnosis: opensme-opencloud claims a static IP on opensme-net (traefik depends on it); postgres is dynamic and grabbed the address while opencloud was down after a host/docker restart — opencloud then cannot bind its static IP. The disconnect/reconnect of postgres also DROPS its netns name alias, which caused zitadel database errors afterwards.
remediation: docker network disconnect opensme-net opensme-postgres
docker compose up -d --no-deps opencloud to reclaim the static address
Re-attach postgres and RESTORE the name alias: docker network connect --alias postgres opensme-net opensme-postgres
Verify zitadel can reach postgres again (alias restored) before declaring done
